summary_paragraph: A woman with prior Roux-en-Y gastric bypass and gastrostomy tube dependence presented with several days of non-bloody diarrhea with cramping and symptoms of dehydration. She was admitted to the bariatric surgery service, treated with intravenous fluids and initial bowel rest (NPO), and monitored for recurrent symptoms given her history of prior C. difficile colitis. Abdominal imaging showed no evidence of obstruction, and she improved clinically with resolution of significant diarrhea and stable labs. Tube feeds were resumed and tolerated, oral intake was advanced without nausea or vomiting, and a stool C. difficile PCR obtained during the stay was negative. She was discharged home ambulatory and mentally clear with instructions on hydration, symptom monitoring, and outpatient follow-up with her bariatric providers.
